description: Hi, I’m Shahriar, leader of Globe Guardians. We’re building Shake Station: a snow-globe Mars outpost game where players spend Sun Coins on oxygen, food, heat and shielding to keep astronaut Pip alive through storms and solar flares. We’re six (dev, UI/UX, AI, research, video) and need a game dev, NASA data fan, educator, illustrator and tester. Beginners welcome! Shake the globe. Survive the sky.
summary: Shake Station is an interactive Mars survival simulator and Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer built for learners of all ages. Players manage a miniature Martian outpost inside a snow globe, keeping an astronaut buddy named Pip safe over 10 Martian sols. Each day, players allocate solar-generated "Sun Coins" across life support, greenhouse crops, radiation shielding, and scientific discovery, storing excess energy in a battery. Incorporating real NASA datasets—including Curiosity RAD surface radiation measurements, DONKI and SDO solar flare records, Perseverance MOXIE oxygen data, and the 2018 global dust storm—the game simulates realistic space weather hazards and 12-minute Earth communication delays. When a mission fails, a Black Box cause-chain replay helps players analyze engineering trade-offs, transforming complex spaceflight challenges into an engaging, hands-on educational experience.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

Shake Station is a web-based interactive Mars mission simulator and Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer built around a snow-globe outpost at Gale Crater. Over a 10-sol mission, players keep an astronaut buddy named Pip alive by managing daily solar energy ("Sun Coins") across four critical systems: Life Support, Greenhouse Food Crops, Radiation Shielding, and Scientific Discovery. Unspent coins are stored in a battery to survive severe Martian dust storms when solar power drops. Players also contend with solar flares and realistic 12-minute Earth-to-Mars light-speed communication delays. At the end of each sol, players receive an interactive flip-postcard containing verified NASA science facts, and if a mission fails, a Black Box cause-chain replay helps them analyze what went wrong.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Spaceflight engineering involves complex trade-offs between power budgeting, crew safety, and scientific exploration. Shake Station translates these real-world NASA mission challenges into intuitive, cause-and-effect decisions for children, students, and learners of all ages. By linking gameplay directly to authentic NASA datasets, it fosters STEM literacy, critical thinking, and spatial weather awareness without requiring prior technical background.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used:

- Frontend & Game Engine: HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (zero external game engine dependencies for fast, lightweight cross-device performance).

- Graphics & Audio: Custom responsive SVG illustrations, CSS keyframe animations, and cross-platform Web Audio unlock routines.

- Data Integration: Embedded verified snapshots from NASA DONKI, SDO, Curiosity RAD, Perseverance MOXIE, and the 2018 Mars Global Dust Storm, alongside an optional live 7-day solar flare check via the NASA CCMC DONKI API.

- Hosting & Version Control: GitHub for source control and Vercel for global cloud deployment.

Creativity & Key Design Factors Considered:

Our team ("Team Globe Guardians") framed the Martian habitat inside a tactile "snow globe" metaphor ("Shake the globe. Survive the sky.") to make planetary survival immediately approachable and memorable for young learners. Key factors we prioritized included cross-device responsiveness (desktop, tablet, and mobile), accessibility (reduced-motion toggle, high-contrast cockpit HUD, clear visual/audio feedback), and strict scientific transparency by clearly tagging embedded NASA snapshots versus live telemetry.
